query: I'm considering graduate school but I can't afford to quit my job. Should I do part-time or full-time?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, US News, USA): Part-time graduate programs have expanded significantly and now include many top-ranked schools — for professional degrees like MBA, MPA, or MS in professional fields, part-time outcomes are largely equivalent to full-time.

Source 2 (2022, Georgetown Center on Education, USA): Full-time graduate students complete their degrees faster, build stronger peer networks, access more research and internship opportunities, and report higher satisfaction — the immersion advantage is real but expensive.

Source 3 (2023, Reddit r/GradSchool, USA): Community advice is heavily context-dependent — for research-based degrees (PhD, academic MA), full-time is essentially required due to advisor relationships and lab requirements; for professional degrees, part-time is often viable.

Source 4 (2022, GMAC MBA Programs, USA): Part-time MBA students who maintain employment during their degree have higher post-graduation salaries than full-time students on average — they apply learnings immediately and graduate without employment gap.

Source 5 (2021, Inside Higher Ed, USA): Part-time degree completion rates are significantly lower than full-time — working adults consistently underestimate the difficulty of sustained multi-year part-time study alongside full-time employment and family obligations.
atoms: perspective: Student pursuing a research-based or academic degree
perspective: Student with employer tuition reimbursement
perspective: Working professional pursuing a professional degree
plausible_answers: Do a part-time professional degree (MBA, MPA, MS), since you maintain income, apply learning immediately, and outcomes largely match full-time.
Go full-time if you can fund it, since peer network, research access, and immersion are hard to replicate part-time.
Pursue part-time only with employer tuition reimbursement, since without it the burnout risk over 3–4 years is high.
